text:
maya: Heads up — noticed a huge gap in traces for async workers after the gateway -> queue refactor. worker spans show up as new root spans instead of children.

jon: saw that too. lots of orphaned traces in Tempo. started around the deploy on monday.

maya: flow recap: client -> gateway (http) -> publish to kafka/sqs -> worker consumes -> db/external calls. gateway sets W3C headers on HTTP but we aren't copying trace context into message headers consistently.

ashish: do we have a standard for message propagation? I thought we used x-correlation-id for everything.

maya: we do, but correlation-id isn't enough for distributed tracing (no span ids, sampling decision, tracestate).

kai: quick proposal: always propagate W3C traceparent + tracestate into message headers (Kafka headers, SQS message attributes). baggage kept minimal. For systems that forbid arbitrary header names, use a tiny envelope header like x-rd-trace (base64 json).

lena: +1 but watch size limits. message attribute/header size varies by broker. keep the envelope compact: traceparent, tracestate (optional), sampling flag. avoid full baggage.

jon: also need to respect sampling decisions set by the gateway. workers must not unilaterally force-sample unless there's a debug override. otherwise we double-count and blow retention.

maya: right — sampling bit should be propagated. we can use the traceparent sampled bit plus an explicit x-rd-sampled for debug overrides. collector can treat x-rd-sampled=2 as always keep.

ashish: what about retries / older messages? if a message is consumed long after it was produced, the original parent span would be finished. Do we create a new root or link to the original?

kai: OTEL has Links for this. Rule suggestion: if traceparent present and timestamp < now - reparent_threshold (e.g., 5m) -> start new span and add Link to the original trace/span id. If within threshold -> continue as child with remote parent.

lena: small nuance: some exporters (Tempo) join on trace id; to preserve causal chains we should keep trace id constant if possible. even when linking, use the same trace id but new span id.

jon: implementation note: SDKs differ on how to create remote parent vs link. we'll need a small helper lib (go/python/node) that hides this.

maya: suggested envelope format (keeps header parsing simple):

```{"tp":"00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01","ts":"rd=1","s":"1","t":1610000000}```

base64 -> x-rd-trace header. fields: tp=traceparent, ts=tracestate, s=sampled (0/1/2), t=epoch producer ts.

ashish: envelope is fine but I'd prefer raw traceparent + tracestate when possible. envelope as fallback for SQS/older clients.

jon: tests to add in PR: publish from gateway with trace headers -> consume in worker -> assert child span has same trace id and parent span id matches gateway span id when within threshold. also test link-case when producer ts is old.

tracebot: :rotating_light: alert: Missing trace context detected — 34k kafka messages without traceparent in kafka-prod last 24h.

maya: ouch. that explains the spike.

lena: ok action items: @jon prototype a small shim for kafka consumer/producer and sqs adapter that normalizes context (create PR by EOW). @ashish update gateway client libs to inject either raw W3C headers or x-rd-trace envelope. @kai add link/reparent logic to worker tracer util (configurable threshold). I'll draft the telemetry retention/sampling playbook (how collectors treat x-rd-sampled) and circulate.

jon: will do. i'll include e2e test and a simple bench for header overhead.

ashish: i'll also update docs and add a migration note for older services. we should roll this as a minor across prod regions with feature flag.

maya: thanks team. let's sync on Wed 10am to review the PR and infra quota/retention implications.

jon: fwiw putting traceparent everywhere fixed a similar issue in payments last year. low-risk change if we keep baggage tiny.

kai: one last thought: for high-throughput hot paths we can compress the envelope (tiny binary form) and keep an internal header encoder/decoder. follow-up after the initial rollout.

lena: copying telemetry eng so they're aware of collector-side sampling implications.

maya: done. :thumbsup:
